zero_retry_decision_challenged.fanin_decision: max_retry_budget = 0 for all eight sources, preserved-from-C4B list retained verbatim
zero_retry_decision_challenged.challenge: Does zero retry accidentally conflict with a previously frozen required retry law?
reasoning: C4B's frozen retry/stop law contains five clauses. Four are prohibitions (no automatic fallback/guessing/substitution; immediate stop on hash/config/authority/oracle mismatch; Candidate A/B/C and measured P2X outside the warrant; no excluded source opened). None of these is violated by a zero budget; a zero budget makes them unreachable rather than lax.

The fifth clause, 'Retries must be separately counted and reason-coded; a retry may not change source, encoding, variables, operations, or authority', is a GOVERNANCE clause conditioned on a retry occurring. It is not an authorisation of any retry. A budget of zero is compatible: the count is 0 and requires no reason code.
C4B set NO numeric retry budget anywhere in its template. There is therefore no frozen numeric value for the fan-in to contradict.

Omega-1 O1-C08 states that 'A corrected execution uses separately bound authority/commit/runtime and the issued new-run/retry law.' This confirms that the retry budget is per-issued-law and that any retry requires a new law. The freeze implements exactly this: 'A corrected rerun requires new HQ-bound execution authority and a newly issued warrant.'
Omega-1 O1-C07 requires expected budgets to be frozen before launch. Zero is a frozen budget.

The direction of the change is strictly tighter than C4B, which is the fail-closed direction. C4B froze immediate-stop-on-mismatch, so no permitted variation remains that a retry could legitimately explore.
zero_retry_decision_challenged.fanin_disclosure_quote: Every per-source max_retry_budget is 0 because C4B froze immediate-stop-on-mismatch and no permitted variation remains that a retry could legitimately explore. A retry is authorised only by a NEW HQ-bound warrant, never by this one.
zero_retry_decision_challenged.advisory_operational_note: With zero retry and a maximum of one full Route-B pass, a transient environment or I/O failure has no lawful recovery path and would force a full re-warrant cycle. This is correct by design and I record it only so HQ is not surprised by the operational cost.
